scenes.text: Your client's website is finished. But where should it live? Let's pick the right hosting in one minute.
Shared hosting is like renting a room in a big house. It's cheap, easy, and great for small WordPress sites.
The catch? You share one server with hundreds of neighbors, so a traffic spike next door can slow you down.
Static hosting, like Netlify, Vercel, or GitHub Pages, serves plain files from a global network. Often free, and super fast.
Perfect for landing pages and portfolios. But there's no PHP and no database built in.
A VPS is your own apartment: a private virtual server with full control. Ideal for Laravel or custom apps.
But now you're the landlord. Updates, security, and backups are all on you.
Managed WordPress hosting costs more, but experts handle speed, backups, and security, so your client can relax.
And cloud platforms like AWS or Google Cloud can scale to millions of visitors. Powerful, but complex to set up.
Quick guide. Landing page? Go static. Small business WordPress? Shared or managed. Custom app? VPS. Huge traffic? Cloud.
Match the hosting to the project, not the hype. Follow for more web builder tips.
